proposals.evidence: CDIAL 2871 karpaṭa lists Prakrit kappaḍa, Punjabi kappṛā, Marwari kapṛo, Gujarati kāpaṛ and Marathi kāpaḍ “cloth”. It explicitly marks several Nepali/Bihari/Awadhi kapṛā forms as Hindi loans and questions short-vowel Gujarati borrowing; these are held. The addenda also question the older word’s formation.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 11392.2 varṣa gives Prakrit varisa, Hindi baras, Old Marwari barasa, Gujarati varas, Bihari baris and northwestern varh-/varih- forms for “year”. Punjabi varas/baras is explicitly a Central loan; conservative ś/ṣ forms and local retroflex innovations are held rather than inferred automatically.
